name: InstallProductDialog
intent: Four-step product install — draft the target, compute a plan, review release evidence, apply — over a planner that resolves adds, collisions and blockers before anything is written.
when: Installing a first-party product into a project
Any staged operation where a plan must be reviewed before it is applied
whenNot: Installing an end-user app -> use the marketplace install lifecycle

chooseOver.component: A confirm dialog over an install action
chooseOver.because: computeInstallPlan resolves object and name collisions and six blocker codes (permission, dependency, linked, installed, readiness, noop) BEFORE anything is written; a confirm dialog can only ask, not explain.

product.note: null keeps the dialog mounted but inert — the catalogue renders it as an unconditional sibling.

mode.note: Only the title and the recorded lifecycle differ between the two.

installs.note: The live install array; dependency, linked and already-installed checks read it.

persona.note: Every gate is evaluated against the acting persona, live.

onApply.note: Fired with the install record an apply WOULD have written — the dialog mutates nothing.

dataContract.rowIdentity: Products are keyed by productKey; plan entries by apiName.

states.draft: Target and mode chosen; nothing computed yet.
states.plan: Adds, object and name collisions and blockers resolved read-only.
states.blocked: Blockers are visible but never stop navigation — the block is enforced once, on Apply, and only the FIRST blocker is toasted. The flow is a review surface, not a gate.
states.applied: onApply receives the record; the host decides whether to write it.

minimalExample:
import {InstallProductDialog, computeInstallPlan} from "@corensystem/coren-ui/pages/install-product-dialog";

<InstallProductDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} product={product} />
evaluationCriteria: The dialog mutates nothing — apply hands the record to the host.
Blockers do not stop navigation; the block lands once, on Apply.
Every blocker names its code and its reason.

lineage.authoredBy: Promoted from the WC3 product catalogue (2026-08-26)

extracted: install planner with six blocker codes

notes: The planner is the widget's real data contract and was already separable.
Promoted in group B of the missing-widgets template review.

usage: Use InstallProductDialog when you need to display content that temporarily overlays the main interface. This component is useful for focused interactions, confirmations, or supplementary information.
InstallProductDialog should be used sparingly as overlays interrupt the user's workflow. Reserve this component for important interactions that require user attention or action before continuing.

anatomy.description: InstallProductDialog is composed of the following parts:

parts.name: InstallProductDialogTrigger
parts.description: Element that opens the dialog when activated.

parts.name: InstallProductDialogContent
parts.description: Container for the dialog content and overlay.

parts.name: InstallProductDialogHeader
parts.description: Header section containing title and description.

bestPractices.description: Trap focus within the dialog and return focus when closed.

bestPractices.description: Avoid opening dialogs from within dialogs, use sequential flow instead.

bestPractices.title: Provide clear exit
bestPractices.description: Always include a visible close button and support Escape key.

bestPractices.title: Don't trap users
bestPractices.description: Never make dialogs impossible to close or require specific actions to dismiss.
